Divisia monetary aggregates index

Source: R/dmai.R
dmai.Rd

dmai() aggregates monetary assets (currency, deposits, ...) into one index of monetary services. Each component is weighted by its share in the expenditure on monetary services, priced by its user cost (Barnett 1978, 1980): an asset that pays a rate close to the benchmark rate is held mostly as a store of value and gets a small weight, while currency and demand deposits get a large one. The simple sum, which weights every component equally, and the currency equivalent index are given for comparison.

Usage

dmai(
  .data,
  method = c("Barnett", "Hancock", "Fisher", "SimpleSum", "CE"),
  logbase = NULL,
  date = "Date",
  x = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  user_cost = NULL,
  benchmark = NULL,
  percent = TRUE,
  base = 100,
  as_dt = TRUE
)

# Default S3 method
dmai(
  .data,
  method = c("Barnett", "Hancock", "Fisher", "SimpleSum", "CE"),
  logbase = NULL,
  date = "Date",
  x = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  user_cost = NULL,
  benchmark = NULL,
  percent = TRUE,
  base = 100,
  as_dt = TRUE
)

Arguments

.data

a data frame with one row per date: a date column and, for every component, a quantity column and a rate column (named x1, x2, ... and r1, r2, ... unless x and r are given).

method

"Barnett" (default), "Hancock", "Fisher", "SimpleSum" or "CE".

logbase

base of the logarithm of the growth DMAI of the "Barnett", "Fisher", "SimpleSum" and "CE" indexes; NULL (default) for the natural logarithm. Version 0.5.0 used base 10 by default; logbase = 10 reproduces it.

date

name of the date column (default "Date").

x

names of the quantity columns (default NULL: x1, x2, ...).

r

names of the rate columns, in the order of x (default NULL: r1, r2, ...).

user_cost

names of columns that give the user costs directly, in the order of x (default NULL: computed from the rates). The rates are then needed only for "CE".

benchmark

the benchmark rate: NULL (default, the largest component rate), a column name, a number or one value per row of .data, in the units of the rates.

percent

logical; are the rates in percent (default TRUE) or decimal?

base

value of the index at the first date (default 100).

as_dt

logical; TRUE (default) returns the table of the index, as version 0.5.0 did; FALSE returns the full result.

Value

With as_dt = TRUE, a data.table with the date, DMAI (the growth in percent, NA at the first date), index and value (the index in the units of x, equal to the simple sum at the first date). With as_dt = FALSE, an object of class c("dmai_index", "dmai_result", "list") with index (that table), components (quantities, rates, user costs and shares by date), benchmark, price (expenditure and dual price index), moments (see dmai_moments()), simple_sum, fisher (Laspeyres and Paasche links, for "Fisher") and settings. print(), plot(), ggplot2::autoplot() and dmai_interpret() apply.

Details

With quantities \(x_{it}\) of components \(i = 1, \dots, n\) at dates \(t\), their rates of return \(r_{it}\) and the benchmark rate \(R_t\), the user cost of component \(i\) is $$\pi_{it} = \frac{R_t - r_{it}}{1 + R_t}$$ (Barnett 1978) and its expenditure share \(s_{it} = \pi_{it}x_{it} / \sum_j \pi_{jt}x_{jt}\). With \(\bar{s}_{it} = (s_{it} + s_{i,t-1})/2\), the methods are

"Barnett"

the Divisia index in the discrete form of Tornqvist and Theil (Barnett 1980): $$\log\frac{Q_t}{Q_{t-1}} = \sum_i \bar{s}_{it}\left(\log x_{it} - \log x_{i,t-1}\right).$$

"Hancock"

the same shares with simple growth rates (as in version 0.5.0): $$\frac{Q_t}{Q_{t-1}} - 1 = \sum_i \bar{s}_{it}\left(\frac{x_{it}}{x_{i,t-1}} - 1\right).$$

"Fisher"

the Fisher ideal index, the geometric mean of the Laspeyres and Paasche indexes with the user costs as prices (Fisher 1922; Diewert 1976): $$\frac{Q_t}{Q_{t-1}} = \left(\frac{\sum_i \pi_{i,t-1}x_{it}}{\sum_i \pi_{i,t-1}x_{i,t-1}}\cdot\frac{\sum_i \pi_{it}x_{it}}{\sum_i \pi_{it}x_{i,t-1}}\right)^{1/2}.$$

"SimpleSum"

the official aggregate \(\sum_i x_{it}\).

"CE"

the currency equivalent index \(\sum_i (R_t - r_{it})x_{it}/R_t\) (Rotemberg, Driscoll and Poterba 1995; Barnett 1991).

All indexes are chained and equal base at the first date. The growth DMAI is \(100\log(Q_t/Q_{t-1})/\log(\mathrm{logbase})\), in percent for the natural logarithm, and \(100(Q_t/Q_{t-1} - 1)\) for "Hancock".

The benchmark rate is the largest rate of the components at each date when benchmark = NULL (as in version 0.5.0; that component then has a user cost of zero), or the given benchmark, raised to the largest component rate where it is lower (the upper envelope). The factor \(1/(1 + R_t)\) is common to the components and does not change the shares.

The dual user-cost price index follows by factor reversal, \(P_t = E_t / V_t\), with the expenditure \(E_t = \sum_i \pi_{it}x_{it}\) and the aggregate \(V_t\) in the units of \(x\) (column value).

References

Barnett, W. A. (1978). The user cost of money. Economics Letters, 1(2), 145–149. doi:10.1016/0165-1765(78)90051-4

Barnett, W. A. (1980). Economic monetary aggregates: an application of index number and aggregation theory. Journal of Econometrics, 14(1), 11–48. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(80)90070-6

Diewert, W. E. (1976). Exact and superlative index numbers. Journal of Econometrics, 4(2), 115–145. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(76)90009-9

Hancock, D. (1985). The financial firm: production with monetary and nonmonetary goods. Journal of Political Economy, 93(5), 859–880. doi:10.1086/261339

Rotemberg, J. J., Driscoll, J. C. and Poterba, J. M. (1995). Money, output, and prices: evidence from a new monetary aggregate. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 13(1), 67–83.

Examples

data(money_sim)
d <-
  dmai(
      .data     = money_sim
    , method    = "Barnett"
    , logbase   = NULL
    , date      = "Date"
    , x         = NULL
    , r         = NULL
    , user_cost = NULL
    , benchmark = "rb"
    , percent   = TRUE
    , base      = 100
    , as_dt     = TRUE
    )
d

fit <-

fit
